articleTitle: Integrated active antennas on silicon
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Integrated active antennas have been designed, fabricated, and used as low-cost front-ends for sensor and communication applications in the frequency bands around 61 and 76.5 GHz allocated for industrial and vehicular applications. The active antenna concept, i.e. the spatial integration of antenna and active element, results in minimization of the required chip size, high reproducibility, and, thus, low costs. The design of active millimeter wave antennas with respect to the impedance matching of antenna and active element as well as the radiation characteristics is discussed. The fabrication process on high resistivity silicon substrates is presented. Application of these front-ends in radar and communication systems is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Schottky contact between metal and two-dimensional electron gas: device applications to low-noise optical detectors
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The current-voltage behaviour of a modified metal-semiconductor-metal (MSM) structure based on direct contact to an AlGaAs-GaAs heterojunction is presented. An analytical description of Schottky contact between metal and the two-dimensional electron gas (2-DEG) and its effects on current transport are investigated to better understand device operation. Thermionic emission calculations lead to a barrier enhancement factor of exp(-E/sub 0//k/sub B/T). The new device demonstrates reduction in dark current as well as higher responsivity and lower reach-through voltage.

articleTitle: Analysis of chaff cloud RCS applying fuzzy calculus
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This work provides an insight to the application of fuzzy theory to evaluate chaff cloud RCS, /spl sigma//spl I.cap/. First it describes a model for /spl sigma//spl I.cap/, and then some of the parameters are taken as fuzzy. It also indicates how the effectiveness of a chaff system against specific threats can be assessed by means of a belief function. Furthermore, before the conclusions, it comments on a technique to evaluate /spl sigma//spl I.cap/ when only fixed frequency radars are available.

articleTitle: Neural model of electrical devices for circuit simulation
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this work, a neural model for nonlinear circuit devices is proposed. This is an alternative to the modeling of complex ill-defined input-output mapping in new, not well-known structures. The neural model has been used in simulation algorithms revealing good approximation and generalization performance. The model is also been used to estimate output derivatives, which are needed in some simulation and optimization algorithms.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic study of coupling between active and passive circuits
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In recent years, because of the high density of microwave circuits and the rise of frequency, the conception of global simulators is being studied more and more in many laboratories. These simulators take into account the direct electromagnetic influence between the currents in the active parts of circuits (generally localized) and the passive components (distributed in lines or radiating patches). The modelisations used are of differents types such as finite elements, finite differences in time domain, and integral approaches. Firstly, the author shows how the active elements are taken into account in the different electromagnetic modelisations. The efficiency of a global simulation in relation to the classical representation is demonstrated for a particular case. Secondly, the author's attention is devoted to a rigorous definition and analysis of sources and active elements in integral methods, which are particularly well adapted for the conception of global simulators. Finally, some examples are given.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave devices based on dielectric, ferrite and semiconductor waveguides
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A set of passive and active devices based on dielectric, ferrites and semiconductors for the frequency ranges 26-48, 80-120, and 115-145 GHz have been created and investigated. These devices use dielectric strip waveguides, image waveguides, nonradiative waveguides of rectangular cross-section and provide optical or magnetic control of attenuation, phase and polarization. The advantages of the reported devices are as follows: broad band, simple construction, small dimensions, low weight and cost. Receiving, transmitting and measuring systems using above mentioned devices were realized.

articleTitle: Microchip laser for microwave and millimeter-wave generation
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A Nd:LiNbO/sub 3/ microchip laser operating at 1.084 /spl mu/m wavelength was designed, implemented, and characterized. The laser cavity was designed to have a free spectral range (FSR) of 20 GHz and an output optical power greater than 20 mW. By exploiting the electrooptical properties of the lithium niobate host, it was possible to mode-lock the microchip laser at 20 and 40 GHz. With this technique it was possible to optically generate the subcarrier with a high modulation index (95.6%).

articleTitle: RF-front end and optical feeding system for a millimeter-wave broadband communications system at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The paper presents the integration of microwave and millimeter-wave techniques as well as the RF-front end and optical feeding system of a wireless broadband integrated services communications system at 60 GHz. The system is intended for indoor use and integrates applications ranging from low data rate mobiles to high rate portable or fixed stations. Antennas, microwave and MM-wave circuits and new optical components are being developed. A hardware demonstrator for proof of concept is currently being built and will incorporate several features of the entire system.

articleTitle: Passive and remote sensing based upon surface acoustic wave in special environments
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A sensor system and SAW tags used as passive sensing are studied. The incorporation of SAW ID-tag will allow identification for multisensor and wireless sensing of quantities that is difficult to work by conventional method. The unique feature is that it is suitable for remote sensing of physical quantities and can also remote sensing chemical quantities. So, it can be used in the detection of explosive gases and toxic gases.

articleTitle: About simulation of fields in large particles model
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The original method of fields' interpolation between points of a discretization grid in the model of an electron beam is described. In contrast to known methods (nearest grid point, clouds in cell, etc.), interpolation by polynoms with smoothing is used here, which is carried out between points of a four-dimension space-time cell. Polynoms of the first order and the method of least squares are used. This permits one to reduce space and time fluctuations of fields in the transient (time-dependent) model.

articleTitle: A large area, high speed photodetector for a microwave modulated hybrid lidar-radar application
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: For microwave modulated lidar applications, a large area photodetector with low noise, high gain, and a bandwidth of a few gigahertz is needed. The photodetector presented is a vacuum photodiode that employs a planar 300 /spl mu/m/sup 2/ metal-semiconductor-metal device as the anode to increase the response speed. This is the first known use of a metal-semiconductor-metal device under electron bombardment. The photodetector has an 8 mm active area, noise figure less than 1.5 dB, gain greater than 10/sup 3/, and an expected bandwidth exceeding 3 GHz.

articleTitle: A fiber-optic Bragg-grating temperature sensor for high-voltage transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this work a new fiber-optic temperature sensor is proposed. The device is based on Bragg gratings photoinduced on the optical fiber core and it is intended for temperature monitoring of electric power systems and high-voltage transmission lines. In contrast to most published work the sensor does not rely on interferometric techniques. The procedure being proposed employs a dual-wavelength measurement of the optical power being reflected (or transmitted) by a Bragg mirror in order to track temperature variations, simultaneously cancelling spurious readings due to source power fluctuations, fiber attenuation, losses, etc. Preliminary results are presented and a possible experimental implementation is discussed.

articleTitle: Planar array antenna synthesis using genetic algorithms with a penalty function
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper presents the synthesis of a planar array antenna with rectangular cells using genetic algorithms (GAs). GAs are used to calculate the complex excitation coefficients for each element of the array in order to obtain a radiation pattern specified by many constraints. The results show good agreement between the desired and calculated radiation pattern when we use the GA with a penalty function.

articleTitle: Generating fading-resistant constellations using genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this paper Genetic Algorithms (GAs) are used to search sub-optimal fading-resistant constellations. The results show that the use of genetic algorithms is profitable in two aspects. The first is less time expensive and, second, the constellations generated reveal better performance when compared in terms of a figure of merit defined for Rayleigh channels.

articleTitle: Very wideband monolithic transimpedance amplifiers for mass production
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A new full design method for developing high bit rate TIA MMICs to be economically produced in large quantities is described in detail. As an example of the method application, the design is reported of a MMIC TIA for 5 Gbit/s optical receivers, having a new circuit topology which allows outstanding improvements of the receiver bandwidth, noise and dynamic range to be obtained. Finally, the great potential of this topology for future developments of high performance and much faster circuits is briefly outlined.

articleTitle: Diffraction and backcoupling of surface plasmon oscillations in a planar waveguide
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A theoretical approach that accounts for diffraction and backcoupling of surface plasmon (SP) oscillations on a metallized planar waveguide is described. The model explains previously reported experimental studies related to the development of SP based optical fiber sensors and can be used to determine design parameters. Results indicate that a planar waveguide metallization scheme similar to that employed in the single mode fiber configuration is a feasible alternative for the construction of integrated optics sensor devices.

articleTitle: A probabilistic model of rain and ice depolarisation based on the experimental estimation of the atmospheric ice content
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper describes a model to estimate the depolarisation due to ice crystals. The theoretical model is compared with results of measurements performed in Italy using the OLYMPUS and ITALSAT satellites. According to the model, the total ice content is the required parameter to be determined for estimation of the depolarisation. The results of analysis of meteorological database and measurements of the OLYMPUS and ITALSAT beacons, that describe the total amount of ice over Europe and the relationship between rain rate and ice total content, are presented.

articleTitle: Propagation measurements for indoor mobile picocell coverage
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The rapid increase on the demand for mobile telephony has led the operating companies to use cell splitting in order to increase capacity. This tends to reduce the cells sizes to what is called picocells, which suits office and factory environments. Eventually the next generation of mobile systems, PCS, will be introduced, helping to cope with the high demand. Although the frequency of the PCS system will be around 1800 MHz, the aim of this work is to verify how a 900 MHz signal behaves inside a building with corridors and rooms receiving a signal internally and externally. The attenuation due to obstructing material is determined. In the next set of experiments the 1800 MHz frequency will be used.

articleTitle: All-optical soliton switching in three-core nonlinear fiber couplers
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We present an analytical investigation of the propagation and the switching of solitons in a three-core nonlinear fiber coupler with a variational method using the Lagrangian density formulation. The analytical solutions were directly obtained from the coupled nonlinear Schrodinger equations (NLSE). The transmission characteristics of first order solitons obtained by the analytical procedure agrees well with the results obtained from the numerical analysis. In addition the analysis shows the existence of soliton eigenstates in the three core nonlinear fiber coupler, where no coupling between the fibers was observed.

articleTitle: Time domain simulation of NRD guide amplitude modulator
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The numerical simulation of a reflection type amplitude modulator using the NRD guide to propagate carrier and modulated waves is presented. The FDTD technique is used to solve Maxwell's equations while the forward time average differencing approach is applied to circuit equations. Both methods are coupled and the results have shown high quality double side band amplitude modulation.

articleTitle: Use of Green's function approach for low loss SAW filter CAD system development
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Low loss filters based on Single Phase Unidirectional Transducers (SPUDT) could be characterized as a separate class of Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) filters because they overcome the main SAW filters limitation-6 dB bidirectional insertion loss. There are two different physical phenomena which could be used to ensure low loss: acoustic reflection of SAW (used normally for substrate with small piezoelectric coupling coefficient k/sup 2/) and electric SAW regeneration (used for substrate with high k/sup 2/). Although both effects finally give contribution to reflectivity of SAW Interdigital Transducer (IDT), models used to account for them are completely different. For SPUDT on the substrates with small k/sup 2/ COM-theory is used, while for the substrate with high value of k/sup 2/ Green's Function Model (GFM) could be directly used. GFM being applicable to IDT with arbitrary topology has two main disadvantages, namely, it is difficult to find a set of consistent model parameters for practical use and computation time increases in power law with the growth of IDT length reaching very quickly unacceptable values. In this paper we present CAD system for calculation of low loss SAW filters parameters based on GFM. Floquet theorem being used for presentation of filter with long IDT, computation time decreases dramatically. The method developed works both for high and low k/sup 2/ value substrates. Results of calculation of SPUDT characteristics with the help of method proposed are presented.

articleTitle: Rain attenuation prediction for the design of site-diversity LEO/SMS Gateway configuration in the tropics
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper presents a propagation analysis regarding the set up of a LEO/SMS Gateway in a tropical region. The propagation effects considered are rain induced attenuation and gaseous absorption. The study is based on five years measurements of point rainfall rate and slant-path rain attenuation at 12 GHz performed in Rio de Janeiro. A method was developed and applied to scale the measured attenuation results to 19 and 29 GHz, the down and up-link frequencies of the Gateway.

articleTitle: A 15 GHz low cost wireless transceiver
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper reports the investigation on a low cost transceiver for use in point-to-point wireless infrastructure systems operating in the frequency range 14.2 to 15.4 GHz. The issues and tradeoffs encountered when designing a high frequency radio on soft board materials are thoroughly discussed and the main experimental results are presented. A direct modulation system is used in the transmitter, which is capable of delivering an output power of +22 dBm. The receiver noise figure is better than 3.6 dB with a conversion gain of 20.0 dB.

articleTitle: An accurate method for computing BER of a digital optical system through Gaussian approximation
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A new method for the semi-analytical estimation of the BER of digital optical systems is presented. It is based on system simulation and accurately considers the performance degradation caused by waveform distortion. The method profits from the simplicity of Gaussian approximation for noise statistics, though explicitly accounting for ISI effects in noise during the BER estimation. Optically preamplified and APD receivers are considered, for which signal-dependent noise components are dominant. The system parameters influence on receiver sensitivity is studied.

articleTitle: Digital optical transmission links with in-line erbium doped fiber amplifier chains
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A digital optical transmission link with an in-line EDFA chain is analyzed, through computer simulation and semi-analytical BER expressions. Firstly, a link with a single in-line EDFA is considered. The effect of amplifier position on receiver sensitivity is studied. Then, an amplifier chain is examined. The influence of the EDFA chain characteristics on system performance is investigated: amplifier gain, noise figure and spacing are considered. The trade-offs between EDFA parameters and system optimization are addressed.

articleTitle: Microwave And Optoelectronics Education And Research In Canada
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave propagation in general multimode waveguide structures exhibiting simultaneously attenuation, dispersion and coupling phenomena
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A power flow equation describing the power flow of electromagnetic waves in a real multimode waveguide represented by a linear multichannel transmission system exhibiting an attenuation, dispersion, and an interchannel interaction is solved in three iterative ways. In the case of constant attenuation and constant propagation velocities in all channels and for the convolution interchannel interaction, a closed analytical solution of the problem is presented. Interesting forms of the solution, transfer function, and impulse response of the system which enable us to separate and compare the attenuation, dispersion, and coupling effects independently of each other are derived. The transfer function, the impulse response, and excitation conditions for their measurements are further discussed. Relations which make it possible to compare different experimental data obtained under specific excitation conditions in various laboratories are determined. Finally, a linear system with memory at time is studied and it is shown that the real multimode waveguide as a linear multichannel transmission system can be considered as a general linear system with memory at space.

articleTitle: An overview of the RF heating process in the petroleum industry
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The use of electromagnetic heating of petroleum reservoirs has been studied theoretically and also tested in the field. Some of them have produced encouraging results. This heating process appears to be technically attractive, due to the volumetric reservoir heating by radio frequency energy as a result of dielectric losses in the zones containing water. A brief survey of field and laboratory applications is presented with their technical aspects and limitations for the frequency range of 60 Hz to several gigahertz. In particular, various electrode configurations, power levels and frequencies in both field work and laboratory scale are presented. The results indicate that this new technology is attractive, but technological challenges still remain.

articleTitle: A high-power 32 GHz pulsed gyrotron
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We report on the operating characteristics of a 32 GHz pulsed gyrotron that has been designed and built at the Associate Plasma Laboratory of INPE. Experimental results include frequency and power measurements on resonant modes TE/sub 5.1/, TE/sub 2.2/ and TE/sub 0.2/. Measured frequencies are in close agreement with the self-consistent calculated values and power measurements were made using a fast response calorimeter with a sensitivity of 0.1/spl deg/C/Wmin. Results are presented for beam voltages from 30 to 40 kV and electron beam current up to 5.0 A. In single TE/sub 2.2/-mode operation at 30.38 GHz an output peak power of 6 kW was obtained with an overall efficiency of 18%.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna design using the TTL method
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The rectangular-patch antenna and the transformer quarter-wavelength for antenna matching are presented in this work using the full wave model of the Transverse Transmission Line-TTL. This method provides an accuracy result for the patch parameters and is rigorous. It is an efficient method when used with lossy semiconductor or lossless dielectric substrates.

articleTitle: Tensile strength of high speed proof tested fiber optics
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Using the "Statistical Theory of Fracture for Brittle Materials" and performing tests for long lengths of fibers at distinct proof stresses and different velocities, the performance of a high velocity test machine and detected level of damage in the fiber samples, are assessed. To confirm the damage and to know the strength of the fiber samples after proof tests, tensile tests were performed.

articleTitle: Complete nomenclature of symmetrical electromagnetic two-ports with gyrotropic media
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: By using formalism of the point magnetic groups, eight possible scattering matrices of symmetrical two-ports with gyrotropic media are obtained. The magnetic groups of symmetry which generate these matrices are defined. The properties of the two-ports and possibilities of the realization of some electromagnetic functions on the basis of such two-ports are discussed.

articleTitle: A neural adaptive array antenna to reduces interference signals in communications systems
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We consider arrays of elements equally spaced on a linear disposition. Our purpose is to determine the excited elements which optimize the signal interference ratio of an array. The problem of minimizing the signals received from interfering or undesirable signal sources by appropriately modifying the antenna radiation pattern is addressed. A neural network is used to arrive at an optimum set of array excitations to achieve a specified radiation pattern. A linear array antenna with six elements was proposed to evaluate the performance of the neural network controller for reducing interference.

articleTitle: Highly doped n-type silicon theoretical optimization
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Considering the recent modification of n-type highly doped silicon parameters, this work has been based on one-dimensional models with analytical solutions. In order to obtain a good accuracy, a fifth order approximation has been considered. Passivated emitters with a Gaussian profile of n/sup +/pp/sup +/ solar cells were optimized. According to our results, emitter solar cells show their best efficiencies (/spl eta//spl cong/21.60-21.70%) with N/sub s/=1/spl times/10/sup 19/-5/spl times/10/sup 18/ (cm/sup -3/) and (1.2-2.0) /spl mu/m emitter thickness range.

articleTitle: Infrared wireless indoor channels characterisation in asymmetrical rooms
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: An analysis is accomplished of unitary impulse response to the asymmetric channels in optical communications using infrared with diffuse reflection. This is be used in computational studies on the characterization of the wireless indoor infrared channel with multiple path propagation.

articleTitle: New method of computation of electrical Y-matrix for arbitrary connected multielements SAW devices
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We treat SAW devices as an arbitrary multielement system. To describe this system, modified form of chain matrix (E-matrix) is introduced. E-matrix has a propriety of turning the calculation of the transfer matrix of this system into a simple multiplication procedure. This allows to perform computation of electrical response of almost any type of SAW device, since the total transfer matrix could be reduced into a Y-matrix. Examples and simulation results confirming method described are shown.

articleTitle: Application of boundary element method to the analysis of cutoff wavenumbers of ridged rectangular waveguides and ridged circular waveguides
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The computation of the cutoff wavenumbers using the boundary element method (BEM) is presented in this paper. Through discretization, the scalar integral equation Green's function is used to determine the spectrum mode in the ridged waveguide. These equations are transformed into a eigenvalue equation, with the eigenvalues as the resonant frequencies, using the Galerkin method. Electric field plots are presented for ridged rectangular waveguides and ridged circular waveguides. Results are given and compared with published data.

articleTitle: Some experimental results for the head/hand effects in personal communications
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this work, some experimental results for the head/hand effects in personal communications are presented, for the real situation of a person during a call in the AMPS system. The hand-held unit has a monopole antenna. A simple measurement procedure is described and experimental results are discussed including biological effect aspects and wireless communication system performance. The experimental procedure and obtained results instigate other researchers to persue a better characterization of the head/hand-handset interaction in personal communication systems.

articleTitle: Microwave passive power limiters with MESFETs
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper describes design, fabrication and test of various microwave passive power limiters based on GaAs MESFETs. Transistors are used as devices under DC voltage control as well as self-controlled devices. Different limiters and their characteristics are compared.

articleTitle: Heterojunction bipolar transistor technology for defense and commercial applications
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: GaAs heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) have undergone a transition from defense applications to low cost, high volume commercial products for the portable wireless market. In particular, GaAs HBTs have traditionally targetted the front-end interface for RF transceivers, but their insertion has broadened to encompass demodulation, frequency conversion, digitization and clock-recovery functions. As GaAs HBTs establish their presence in the commercial arena, new device technologies are emerging offering better performance and innovative system and circuit options.

articleTitle: An original and rigorous approach to the design of microwave active circuit
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The real frequency technique (RFT) is an efficient numerical method to design matching networks of microwave active circuits. It provides several advantages over most of the usual techniques. Directly including measured scattering and noise parameter data, it does not require any rational functions or circuit models. Moreover, neither a pre-determined matching circuit topology is necessary. The described method also allows designing stability-guaranteed broadband circuits when employing potentially unstable transistors. With the Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm, the RFT can be applied to simultaneously optimize transducer power gain, input and output VSWRs, noise figure and group delay of a multistage microwave active circuit. Applications as different as low-noise amplifiers, active filters or broadband amplifiers are possible.

articleTitle: Optical fiber temperature sensor for microwave hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: An optical fiber thermometer for microwave hyperthermia applications was developed. The probe head uses a standard single mode fiber with a short bend radius covered with silicone elastomer. The prototype has adequate operational characteristics for such applications: accuracy of 0.25/spl deg/C, 0.1/spl deg/C resolution and operational range from 20/spl deg/C to 60/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: Microstrip patch antennas on uniaxial anisotropic substrates with several optical axis orientations
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The characteristics of microstrip patch antennas on uniaxial anisotropic substrates are presented. The analysis was developed in the Fourier domain, by using a combination of the Hertz vector potentials and Galerkin method, to determine the resonant frequency and the Q-factor. The radiation pattern is obtained by using the phase stationary condition. In the anisotropic material, the optical axis orientation is considered to be along the microstrip main axes. For particular cases, the results are in agreement with those available in the literature.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of an integrated laser modulator
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In an Integrated Laser Modulator (ILM), residual optical feedback can lead to a significant level of frequency chirp compared to the case of a discrete external modulator. We have developed an original model of the ILM which has been successfully used in the design and optimisation of the ILM. It allows the calculation of static and dynamic properties of the ILM, aiming at a higher output power while keeping the amount of optical frequency chirp as low as possible. This has been obtained on a new ILM generation for which the output power has been multiplied by two by reducing the DFB coupling coefficient. System experiments at 10 Gb/s have demonstrated transmission distance over 76 km without any optical amplifier. The model shows that the chirp depends on the phase of the modulator and laser facets, in agreement with experimental results. Despite the random character of the phase, a low modulator facet reflectivity (/spl les/2/spl times/10/sup -4/) guarantees low feedback induced frequency chirp. Numerical simulation of the response (power and frequency chirp) to a 16-bit pseudo random bit NRZ sequence at 10 Gb/s has been performed.

articleTitle: Analysis of optical waveguides using Mathematica (R)
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A Notebook developed in the Mathematica software using a rigorous formulation to analyze planar optical waveguides operating in the TE or TM mode is presented. By using the Mathematica facilities, it is possible to simplify the development for the calculation and visualization of the propagation constants and the field distribution. The user can specify the physical and geometrical waveguides parameters or use a set from a practical model library, including MQW waveguides. In this case, the results can be obtained from rigorous analysis or from approximations that reduce the MQW waveguide to an equivalent three-layer slab waveguide.

articleTitle: A coupler with losses in millimetre waves
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: An electromagnetic application to obtain the coupling parameters of the unilateral fin lines coupler asymmetric in the E-plane, with semiconductor substrate is presented. The effective dielectric constant, the attenuation constant and the characteristic impedance, for the odd and even-modes excitation are obtained by Transverse Transmission Line method-TTL. Computer programs, developed in FORTRAN 77 language, given the results of the coupling in 3-D, obtained as function of the frequency, conductivity and permittivity. These results are compared with references and present good agreement.

articleTitle: The use of detectors instead power meters: a simple and cheap option in microwave measurements
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this work, the use of microwave detectors (Schottky diodes) instead power meters is suggested. With this simple substitution, microwave measurements may achieve an easier and cheaper process. The detector specifications are described. In order to exemplify the proposed substitution, experimental results are presented and, when compared to numerical ones, a good agreement is observed. The stability and the price of the detector are some of the advantages of the suggested substitution.

articleTitle: Telecommunication R&D within a competition environment
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The key discriminatory agent for competition among the public telecommunication operating companies lies in the technological innovation in network evolution and the diverse offered services. The generation of innovation by means of technological research and development has now been concentrated on the operating companies in contrast with yesterday's approach when technology generation was strongly in the hands of the industries. In this paper the TELEBRAS Research and Development Center offers its experience in technological innovation in the area of telecommunications by reporting the transformation taking place in its operational approach born from the changes in the scenarios of the governmental and entrepreneurial policies.

articleTitle: Reflection of waves from a strong scatterer buried in a random media
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Reflection of waves from a mirror covered by a random layer of isotropic, absorbing scatterers is studied, and the annular distribution of the scattered intensity is calculated both analytically and numerically. It is shown that backscattering enhancement as well as an enhancement of the incoherent signal in the specular direction take place even in the singly scattered random field. The dependence of the retroreflected intensity is shown to be a non-monotonic function of the depth of the mirror, with a maximum at a depth of order of the scattering mean free path. Possibilities for employing the results obtained to detect buried strong scatterers and to retrieve parameters of the random media are discussed. In particular, it is shown that in the case of strong absorption the reflecting plane manifests itself by the presence of a peak in the retroreflected intensity which is missing from the scattering diagram of a free standing or an infinitely thick random layer.

articleTitle: Global descriptions of digitalized terrain data for propagation studies in rural environments
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Implementation of pseudospline interpolating functions for global modelling of surfaces, as defined by digitalized terrain data, is explored with a view towards its application to propagation studies in rural environments. Due to their inherent properties, pseudosplines are shown to require a reduced number of data points for proper surface representation with consequent alleviation of storage and processing time demands.

articleTitle: An impedance model for the diffraction by phase screen
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A mathematical model to study the diffuse transmitted fields by a phase screen is formulated in a similar way to the method applied for the scattering calculation by metalic rough surfaces. Micro-optic elements can be designed with such calculations applied to integrated optics.

articleTitle: Analysis techniques for surface acoustic wave devices
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper reviews current surface acoustic wave (SAW) technology and their applications in telecommunications systems. It outlines models that are in widespread use for the design of SAW devices, and describes recent developments in the Green's function formalism.

articleTitle: Deep defects in intermediate temperature molecular beam epitaxy grown GaAs and their role in current transport
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Current transport in molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) GaAs grown at low and intermediate growth temperatures is strongly affected by defects. A model is developed here that shows that tunneling assisted by deep defect states can dominate, at some bias ranges, current transport in Schottky contacts to un-annealed GaAs material grown at the intermediate temperature range of about 400/spl deg/C. It is suggested that reduction of these defects by thermal annealing can explain lower current conduction at high biases in the annealed device as well as higher current conduction at low biases due to higher lifetime. Quenching of current by light in the as-grown material is shown and can also be explained based on occupancy of trap states. Identification of this mechanism can lead to its utilization in making ohmic contacts, or its elimination by growing tunneling barrier layers. This material finds wide-spread use in microwave and optical applications.

articleTitle: Radar scattering: a time-frequency perspective
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Time-frequency analysis is used to study electromagnetic scattering from canonical objects leading to the detection, localization and extraction of response features that result from the object's physical attributes. The time-frequency analysis techniques are motivated by signal representation in phase space, and are formulated using the Bargman transform. Bargman transform techniques allow the phase space to be parametrically represented in terms of complex polynomials, and elliptical filters can be constructed to crop selected areas of the phase plane. The filters are applied to the scattering from spheres and thin wires, and the prominent scattering features are identified and extracted.

articleTitle: Theory, C.A.D. optimization and RF & MW circuits for space use
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Reliable circuits must be produced by the proper utilization of circuit theory and computer aided optimization. This paper presents some results, for an LNA, L-band VCO and IF filter, using these principles. It is also discussed how good models in circuit simulators can provide more than good circuits: they help in the production tuning of manufactured equipment.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic fields in open chirostrip multilayered structures
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper presents an analysis method for open chirostrip multilayered structures. Working in the Fourier domain, expressions for the electromagnetic field components are obtained. Effects of chirality on near and far field components are discussed. The behavior of the electromagnetic field components on the interfaces is also analyzed.

articleTitle: Electrical properties of geological materials in the microwave range
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We introduce a new model to describe the electrical behavior of rocks and soils in a broad frequency range, taking into account the fractal properties of the rough surfaces at the interfaces between the blocking grains (metallic or clay particles) and the electrolyte filling the porous spaces. The model is used to analyze the effect of the imaginary part of the dielectric constant on the propagation of electromagnetic waves in the Earth soil.

articleTitle: Four-wave mixing reduction in a long-haul amplified multichannel optical transmission system
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper presents a study on the Four-Wave Mixing (FWM) phenomenon affecting the performance of long-haul Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) optical transmission systems. A brief introduction on the physical nature of FWM is included. Three strategies to reduce its effects in multi-channel transmission systems are summarized. An application of one of these methods, based on an unequal channel spacings scheme, is included.

articleTitle: Precipitation estimates from an electromagnetic lightning detector data in radiofrequencies
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Cloud-to-ground lightning events were monitored during 1995, by a radiofrequencies electromagnetic detection system located in Belem-PA, Brazil. Simultaneously, the pluviometric precipitation was recorded by a FUESS-type pluviograph, located next to the EM-sensors. The relations between cloud electrification and the growth rate of cloud drops, as well as the rain gush after the occurrence of nearby lightning have been observed for a long time, but so far no satisfactory explanation has been offered for these phenomena. Nevertheless, the evident correlation between the frequency of occurrence of the above mentioned type of lightning and the accumulated precipitation levels observed around Belem, led the authors to try to quantify such a relation. Linear regressions between the number of lightning occurrences and the precipitation measured at monthly and hourly intervals, resulted in close parallel lines. The results presented in this work show that in spite of the theoretical difficulties mentioned, EM lightning detection systems have the practical potential to estimate precipitation, when adjusted for a given area of the Earth.

articleTitle: Angular shift by reflection for super-Gaussian beams
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The angular change of super-Gaussian monochromatic beams reflected from a planar surface (single interface and thin film) are studied This change is shown graphically, as a function of the supergaussianity; index for each polarization. Some conclusions can be obtained to characterize the planar structures and the behaviour of supergaussian monochromatic beams in the reflection on the surface.

articleTitle: A new thermal model for HBT RF circuit simulation
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A simple thermal model for heterojunction bipolar transistors was implemented in the HP EEsof LIBRA simulator. The model is based on a proposed circuit that adjusts the Libra's built-in Gummel-Poon model. Thermal effects are properly simulated, giving a good agreement for DC I-V characteristics, small signal S parameters and for power curves at 1.85 GHz signal. A nonlinear dependency of the thermal effect with RF power is observed on the power curves and is properly modeled.

articleTitle: The use of FDTD in waveguides containing magnetized plasma
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The formulation of the finite difference time domain method (FDTD) for the analysis of propagation characteristic of rectangular waveguides filled with magnetized plasma is presented here. In this formulation the FDTD method is used for the numerical solution of Maxwell's equations in the time domain. As a result, the system of partial differential equations formed by the electric and magnetic field components is replaced by a system of finite difference equations that are solved iteratively. The results presented show a variation of the dispersion characteristics of the structures examined as functions of the plasma parameters.

articleTitle: Dependence of microwave properties of HTS parallel coupled-line type 4-pole bandpass filters on enhanced electrodynamic properties of Ag-doped YBCO films
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We designed and fabricated high temperature superconducting (HTS) 4-pole Tchebyshev bandpass filters (BPFs) fabricated on Ag (5 wt.%, 10 wt.%, and 20 wt.%)-doped YBa/sub 2/Cu/sub 3/O/sub 7-/spl delta// thin films. The measured insertion losses of the filters appeared to interrelate strongly with Ag-doping while center frequency and bandwidth exhibited little change. The filter on Ag (10 wt.%)-doped YBCO film exhibited the lowest insertion loss of 0.22 dB at 37 K at the center frequency of 11.6 GHz. The bandwidth was 400 MHz.

articleTitle: Classes of rectangular waveguide discontinuities having same scattering coefficients
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A class of distinct rectangular waveguide discontinuities having same scattering coefficients is presented based on the comparison between the scattering of a inductive post and a inductive iris, which are solved using the mode-matching technique. These results make it possible to handle different structures by a unique electromagnetic analysis.

articleTitle: Overlapping area between three cells
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper examines the joint statistics of paths to three base stations and estimates the proportion of cell area within which the mobiles are considered to have adequate communication with three or more adjacent base stations in different fading conditions. The calculations are carried out on the instantaneous power basis, in which the signal envelope is assumed to follow the Rayleigh, Lognormal and Suzuki distributions.

articleTitle: Simulation of WDM systems using PC-SIMFO: performance of optical filters
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this paper we use a simulation environment called PC-SIMFO, to evaluate the performance of a WDM system, using five types of optical filters as demultiplexers. The system simulated is a 4-channel intensity modulated and direct detection transmission system. Our results show that it is possible to transmit more than 200 channels at 2.5 Gb/s over 50 km, using conventional single mode optical fiber.

articleTitle: A performance assessment of the Green Bank Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper briefly summarizes the results of a computational study performed to evaluate the electrical performance of the Green Bank Telescope reflector antenna. All computed patterns were obtained with the program PRAC (Parabolic Reflector Analysis Code), developed by the authors, and with the commercial code GRASP7. The patterns and performance values, not published anywhere else as far as the authors know, indicate that low cross polarization (XPOL) performance can be achieved with a dual offset configuration, provided that a low XPOL feed is employed.

articleTitle: Simulation of power control in CDMA cellular system
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Power control in CDMA cellular system is analyzed in detail in this paper. It is well known that power control plays a very important role in CDMA cellular systems. When a mobile subscriber rambles in the cell, especially when very close to the border, the realization of power control is practically based on the result of the detection of pilot signal power, rather than the distance used in the previous analyses. An investigation of this effect is made and results are given in this paper.

articleTitle: Generation and detection of pulsed microwave signals by THz optoelectronics
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A novel electro-optic detection system has be used to characterize the temporal and spatial distribution of free-space broadband, pulsed electromagnetic radiation (MHz/THz beams). We report recent progress in ultrafast optoelectronics in E-field detection application. Basic concepts and preliminary results in the generation, detection, and imaging of pulsed electromagnetic radiation with electro-optic crystals are discussed.

articleTitle: Showcasing Electromagnetics And Optoelectronics: Emc And Fiber Optics In The Bsee Curriculum
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings

articleTitle: Education And Research In Microwave And Millimeter Waves In The Institute Of Radio Engineering And Electronics Ras And Moscow Institute Of Physics And Technology
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave propagation in a periodic array of rectangular dielectric waveguides
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The electromagnetic wave propagation in a two dimensional dielectric grating, consisting of a periodic array of rectangular dielectric waveguides, is examined here using the moment method with an adequate electric field expansion inside each rectangular dielectric waveguide. The free space Green's function is obtained by using the volume equivalence theorem. It includes the waveguide coupling through the use of the Floquet's theorem. Curves of normalized phase constant as functions of Floquet's wavenumber are obtained for various waveguide dimensions. Agreement is observed with existing results in the limit of the one dimensional dielectric grating.

articleTitle: Broadband dual mode couplers with cylindrical posts in rectangular waveguides
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Moment method techniques associated with experimental prototype bench work have made possible to develop a new series of broadband dual mode couplers that can be applied to small antenna feed systems. These couplers incorporate cylindrical posts which can be partially inserted in the main waveguide to act as a filter, or can be fully inserted to reflect all the energy contained on one of the polarization components driving it to the coupling window.

articleTitle: Control of optical properties of materials by atomic coherence and quantum interference effects
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We investigate the spontaneous emission spectrum of a three-level atom coherently driven by a microwave field. The microwave excitation establishes a coherent link between the bottom two levels, and as a consequence induces the quantum interference of previously independent decay pathways. As the decay pathways differ from one another by an odd number of stimulated emission processes, the spontaneous emission spectrum acquires a dependence on the phase of the excitation field, a feature that is absent in other resonance fluorescence phenomena.

articleTitle: Accurate method for the intermodulation analysis of nonlinear microwave circuits
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Accurate prediction of distortion effects is an important point in nonlinear communication systems and device design. As the voltage-controlled current source I/sub d/ is the most dominant nonlinearity in a field effect transistor, we present in this paper an efficient method which determines analytically the intermodulation powers from MESFET I/V characteristics. Based on the characteristic surface technique, the procedure consists of first determining the optimum harmonic loads for the nonlinear element and then, using Volterra series representation, to minimize the corresponding intermodulation powers. The validity of the proposed method was confirmed by comparing the computed values with those presented in technical literature.

articleTitle: Extension of a formula by Harrington which describes the electromagnetic field in a half-space
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In his book "Time-Harmonic Electromagnetic Fields" Harrington (1991) presented a formula which allows the computation of the electric field strength E/spl I.oarr/ in the source-free upper half-space z>0 when only the tangential component E/spl I.oarr//sub t/ on the plane z=0 is given. Different from other authors, we derive this formula from Green's second identity using the technique of scalar Green's function. As an extension also preset sources located at z>0 are considered. Furthermore, with the help of Fourier integrals, we apply Harrington's formula to a domain bounded by two infinite parallel planes. This leads to an infinite system of images and shows the correctness of the formula.

articleTitle: Multilayer anisotropic dielectric grating waveguides
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Frequency selective characteristics of multilayer anisotropic dielectric grating waveguides are analyzed here, having in mind their use as dichroic surfaces in the millimeter waveband. The rigorous formulation described by Costa and Giarola [1993-96] is extended to include biaxial anisotropic dielectrics with their optical axes aligned with the coordinate axes. Numerical results are shown for a sinusoidally varying dielectric constant in the grating. The effect of the dielectric anisotropy square ratio on the resonance anomalies of the diffraction curves is carefully investigated.

articleTitle: Recirculating loop for experimental modeling of long haul communications systems
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We demonstrate an optical fiber recirculating loop for the testing of optical communications systems and devices. The proposed configuration employs sections of dispersion shifted fibers, standard fiber, and a set of inline devices, such as tuning filters, optical amplifiers, polarization controllers, etc. The main results presented here are related to the observation of the effects due to the slow dynamics of optical amplifiers and also to the possibility to simulate extra lengths of fiber with an attenuator.

articleTitle: Wide and flat bandpass tunable optical filter for high-speed wavelength-multiplexed communication systems
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The authors report a tunable bandpass optical filter fabricated with multiple-phase-shifted Bragg resonator based on InGaAs-InP coupled asymmetric quantum wells. The device is very suitable for application in high-speed WDM systems and it is easy to be fabricated.

articleTitle: Eigenmodes in gyrotron coaxial cylindrical resonators with corrugated inner conductor
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A theoretical and experimental investigation on the electrodynamical properties of open coaxial cylindrical resonators with longitudinal slots on the inner conductor wall is carried out as a means to discriminate the total Q/sub T/ factor and resonant frequency of competing modes in high-power gyrotrons. A detailed study of the potentialities of the corrugated coaxial cavity for mode selection in gyrotron cavity is carried out, and, to our knowledge, this is the first time that experiments are performed to verify the theory.

articleTitle: Microwave tunnelling in semiconductor heterostructures through a magnetic barrier
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A new effect is considered-resonance tunneling of microwaves through a magnetic insulating barrier between a selectively doped semiconductor heterostructure and a thick wide-gap semiconductor layer. It is shown the tunneling is due to resonant excitation of coupled spin-electromagnetic surface waves localized at the interface between the magnetic and narrow-gap semiconductor layers. The total tunneling conditions are found for both s- and p-polarized incident waves. The influence of two-dimensional carriers on the microwave tunneling is investigated and coefficients of reflection and transmission are obtained. A new method for determination of 2D-carrier density is proposed.

articleTitle: Microwave applicators for chemical reactions
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Many chemical syntheses of great industrial interest, now occurring in bulky batch reactors, are potential candidates for the use of continuous reactors. A difficult task to perform by conventional continuous methods, for equilibrium reactions. Microwave applications to chemical reactions open up new possibilities in reactor design. Experiments were performed to confirm the basic advantages of microwave application to chemical reactions and a new kind of continuous reactor was developed consisting basically of a continuous microwave applicator coupled to a mechanical device, which permits the extraction of volatile products, without stopping the continuous flow through the reactor.

articleTitle: Compact distributed microwave circuit models generated by the TLM method and systems identification
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We present a method for computer aided design of lumped element equivalent circuits for linear reciprocal distributed microwave circuits. The method is based on a field theoretical analysis of the distributed multiport circuit. It allows one to generate the topology as well as the parameters of the lumped element equivalent circuit after specifying an arbitrary but finite interval of frequencies for the lumped element equivalent circuit.

articleTitle: Evaluation of RZ- and NRZ-format 40 Gb/s transmission over embedded standard fibre employing chirped fibre grating dispersion compensators
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A comparison of the NRZ- and RZ-transmission formats is investigated for 1.55 /spl mu/m 40 Gbit/s dispersion compensated standard fibre transmission. The RZ-format is shown to give a 2-fold increase in transmission distance compared with the conventional NRZ-format. In addition, a larger power margin is allowed. System guidelines are proposed relating the pulse width, equalizer spacing, input power and maximum transmission distance.

articleTitle: Measuring the scattering parameters of microwave devices
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A complete six-port network analyser is proposed that makes use of a single reflectometer. The proposed configuration employes a precision attenuator which dispenses with connections and disconnections with calibration standards, needs no inversion of the two-port device under test for measuring the transmission parameters and as its main feature, avoids the use of switches which are always present in the traditional configurations described in the literature. Its calibration and measurement procedures are also described.

articleTitle: Analysis of highly asymmetric couplers
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The goal of this work is to investigate highly asymmetric couplers as a potential component for monolithic integration. Since most coupled mode formulations available do not attend to requirements such as high refractive index steps, strong coupling, and high propagation losses, a new orthogonal coupled mode approach based on the integral form of the Lorentz reciprocity theorem is formulated. The results obtained with this new approach include the following loss mechanisms: radiation modes, leaky modes, and grating radiation.

articleTitle: Role of fiber length and reflectivity variation on the tunability of an erbium doped-fiber ring laser
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper presents a study of the effects of the doped-fiber length and reflectivity variation in the flatness of the tunability curve of an erbium doped-fiber ring laser. The flat tuning over a broad spectral width is discussed using different couplers and doped-fiber lengths in the ring. The results show that the reflectivity and the doped-fiber length affect the cavity response. We obtain the doped-fiber length and reflectivity which improve the laser performance. The tunability of the device is also improved.

articleTitle: Evaluation of distortion in an overmodulated semiconductor laser through a dynamic model including hysteresis
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: When a semiconductor laser is overmodulated by a sinusoidal current, distortion occurs in the optical signal. Using a static limiter as a first model for the laser only permits a rough analysis of this effect. For describing additional distortion arising when the optical intensity rises above threshold, an improved dynamic model is proposed including an hysteresis.

articleTitle: Force measurement using induced birefringence on Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We experimentally demonstrate the use of Bragg grating reflectors in an intrinsic all fiber polarimetric force sensor. Lateral force applied to the fiber induces a proportional birefringence. If the region in the fiber where the force is applied contains a Bragg grating, it will exhibit two reflection peaks associated with orthogonal polarization modes. The measured force sensitivity was of 7.2/spl times/10/sup -2/ nm/kg for this specific set-up and a very low temperature dependence is expected.

articleTitle: Optical soliton generation using filtering of an external modulated CW laser
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The performance simulation of a high bit rate generator of soliton-like optical pulses is presented. The generator can be implemented using common optical fiber technology. Using a phase modulation of a CW laser, the corresponding spreaded spectrum is conveniently filtered to obtain the high rate pulses that can be controlled by the RF modulating source.

articleTitle: InGaAs/InP CAQW exchange-Bragg resonator based wavelength-selective optical intensity modulator
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We present a novel InGaAs/InP CAQW wavelength-selective optical intensity modulator based on exchange-Bragg resonator. Bandwidth in excess of 100 GHz and low voltage operation, 1.67 V, for an extinction ratio of 20 dB are predicted for a chirp-free modulator.

articleTitle: An educational software for small signal microwave amplifier design
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper describes a new software for solid state microwave amplifier design. The software has been developed for a PC Windows environment with the Borland C++ programming language and using object oriented techniques. All steps of the design of small signal microwave amplifier are supervised by this extensible software: transistor choice, gain and noise analysis, single and multiple frequencies matching, lumped elements and hybrid microstrip and stripline circuit design, and biasing circuits for FET and bipolar transistors. Many kinds of graphics and data files are available for amplifier analysis: transistor s2p data file, input and output constant gain circles for single and multiple frequencies, maximum gain, input and output stability circles, output gain and scattering parameters graphics.

articleTitle: Measurements of chirp and linewidth enhancement factor of DFB semiconductor lasers using a self-homodyne interferometric system
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A self-homodyne interferometric optical system fed by a modulated DFB semiconductor laser is used to obtain the AM and FM response, the chirp parameter and the linewidth enhancement factor of these lasers. Three different DFB lasers were measured and the results are in good agreement with those obtained by others techniques. The knowledge of these lasers characteristics are important in high-performance optical communications systems, to improve the FM response, the transmission data rates, predict channel densities and reduce crosstalk.

articleTitle: Noise performance of HBT as photodetector in analog fiber-optic communication link
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: An analog fiber-optic communication link using a heterojunction bipolar transistor (HBT) as photodetector is analyzed regarding its noise performance Experimental results for signal-to-noise ratio and distortion are compared to other state of the art devices as well as commercial ones. The shot noise limited system using the HBT demonstrated S/N in excess of 50 dB and spurious-free dynamic range better than a commercial PIN. Furthermore, compared to other 3- and 2-terminal devices the HBT is potentially the best candidate for future OEIC technology. Experimental results for a new HBT structure, optimized for photonic applications, shows significant improvement in terms of gain and sensitivity.

articleTitle: In fiber-grating dispersion compensated system using chirped optical pulses
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Dispersion compensated transmission of 43 ps long chirped pulses over 80 km of standard telecommunication fiber is demonstrated. A 100 mm long apodised fiber grating was used. The results show that the control of the chirp of the optical pulses used in transmission systems may not be necessary.

articleTitle: Modeling of an original curved waveguide for microwave filtering applications
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Characterization, parameters analysis and modeling of waveguides devices are three closely related processes presented here over different strategies to provide the results for a microwave filter circuit. The PVM techniques are also used in order to improve the number of simulations necessary for the characterization of the filter device. The expected results of simulation for a four poles Chebyshev filter is obtained. Trends in this kind of association is also discussed generally in this paper.

articleTitle: Radioclimatic parameters for the prediction of multipath fading in radio links in Brazil
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A propagation measurement campaign is being carried out in Brazil to provide long term cumulative distributions of single frequency multipath fading and statistics of the parameters of a two-ray multipath channel model (relative delay and notch depth). The correlation between fade events in consecutive hops in multihop links is also being investigated. Some of the results available are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: On the influence of polysilicon layer resistance upon the noise performance of microwave BJTs
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Different series of double polysilicon bipolar transistors have been characterized in terms of noise and scattering parameters over the 2-6 GHz frequency range at different collector current values, according to their emitter finger number. Extraction of a circuit model has been accomplished for each series based on an improved T-equivalent circuit including noise sources. By such a model, novel analytical expressions for the noise parameters F/sub 0/ (minimum noise figure), |/spl Gamma//sub 0/| (magnitude of the optimum source reflection coefficient) and r/sub n/ (normalized noise resistance) have been derived for this polysilicon self-aligned structure. Following that, a sensitivity analysis has been performed for evaluating the influence of the device model elements upon the noise parameters with specific concern for the polysilicon layer resistance.

articleTitle: SAW filters and technology at CPqD-Telebras
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The increasing interest in SAW devices is noted in different areas of communication. Fiberoptic (SONET and SDH), Personal Communications Systems (PCS), Cordless telephones, Advanced Mobile Phone System (AMPS), Global System for Mobile communication (GSM) and satellites communication systems are ranging from 70 MHz up to 2.5 GHz. For about two decades SAW filters are standard components in every TV IF stage. In radio link systems SAW channel, in IF satellite receivers and spectrum shaping filters are being preferred due to the excellent reproducibility of passband and stopband characteristics. A variety of new SAW structure were developed in order to achieve low insertion loss and high suppression of adjacent interferers. In the RF stage SAW devices compete with others filtering techniques, such as Micro Wave Ceramic (MWC). The use of standardized materials and process decreases fabrication cost and simultaneously increases product quality. Finally, the small size of SAW devices brought a breakthrough in circuit design leading to a growing use of SAW instead of MWC filters. This papers discusses the present and future SAW development at R and D Centre of Telebras.

articleTitle: Multilayer semiconductor substrate in superconducting microstrip lines
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The theory of the multilayer shielded and open microstrip lines considering the superconductor strip on semiconductor regions is presented. The Transverse Transmission Line (TTL) method is used in the analysis. The superconductor effect is included with the boundary condition of the surface impedance, that is related to the complex conductivity of the material, calculated from the advanced two-fluid model. Applying the moment method the complex propagation constant of the structure, including the phase constant and the attenuation constant, is obtained. Results in 2D and 3D are presented for the complex propagation constant, versus the frequency and the temperature, of this multilayer superconducting microstrip lines.

articleTitle: Fast algorithm for the characterization of ridged waveguide discontinuities
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Ridged circular waveguide discontinuities are used in many applications such as polarizers and filters. This paper presents a fast algorithm for their characterization.
