The method is based on integral equation with a scalar Green's function for the calculation of mode spectrum of ridged circular waveguide, in combination with an improved variational multimodal formulation for the characterization of the step discontinuity. The coupling coefficients are evaluated by post-processing of the matrices already used in the mode determination. The overall scattering matrix is obtained by cascading an impedance matrix of each discontinuity. The salient features of this algorithm are its speed and its simplicity. It consumes less memory and CPU time. The numerical results are verified by excellent agreement with measurements.

articleTitle: A new 3D vectorial beam propagation method for optical waveguides
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this paper a novel and efficient 3D vectorial beam propagation scheme, based on the split-operator technique in conjunction with a hybrid vectorial finite element method is reported. The present algorithm takes into account optical waveguides with arbitrary cross-section and inhomogeneous isotropic, lossy media, including metallizations and also nonlinearities.

articleTitle: Numerical schemes for optical soliton propagation analysis: a test comparison
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Recently, a numerical scheme based on a Fourier-Series Approach (FSA) has been proposed to analyse soliton propagation in optical fibres. A test performance has been carried out comparing this novel technique to the widely used Beam Propagation Method (BPM). The remits indicate that the BPM should be preferable for its accuracy, robustness and faster execution.

articleTitle: A low cost design for double offset antenna with spherical main reflector
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper presents the double offset antenna with a symmetrical spherical main reflector, that is a spherical cap, as a low cost configuration for antennas to be used in fixed satellite service ground stations. Electrical performance results for a 3.6 m diameter equivalent aperture antenna designed to work in the FSS Ku band are presented.

articleTitle: Bit error rate performance of high-speed tunnel communication
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The bit error rate performance for high-speed personal communication service in tunnels with and without traffic is investigated. The impulse response of the tunnel is computed by shooting and bouncing ray/image techniques. Binary data with phase shift keying modulation are transmitted over the multipath channel and coherent match filters are used as receivers. The bit error rate for communication in tunnels with and without traffic is calculated. Numerical results have showed that the multipath effect by the vehicles in the tunnel is an important factor for bit error rate performance. In addition, the effect of space diversity techniques on mitigating the multipath fading is also investigated.

articleTitle: Electronics for an experimental 40 Gbit/s OTDM-system
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: For an experimental 40 Gbit/s optical time division multiplexing (OTDM) system, a silicon monolithic integrated circuit was developed which can be operated as a two-output 10 Gbit/s pseudo random data-generator as well as an error-detector and counter. If two circuits are synchronized together, one obtains four m-sequences which can be multiplexed optically to a new m-sequence with the same pattern, but with a data-rate of 40 Gbit/s. After transmission the optical signal is demultiplexed electrically and the total error-rate or the single error-rates of the four channels can be displayed.

articleTitle: A reflector antenna synthesis for proposed Brasilsat B3 South American coverage at C and Ku-bands
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: A shaped reflector antenna synthesis, making, use of physical-optics diffraction in conjunction with a pseudospline global description of the reflector surface is presented for the proposed C and Ku-bands coverage of the South American territory by BRASILSAT B3 satellite. Unique features of the synthesis technique are shown to substantially reduce the computational effort to attend specified main and exterior bounds of coverage areas at two frequencies of the chosen band of operation simultaneously.

articleTitle: Multi-wavelength optical source based on amplified spontaneous emission of erbium doped fiber
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: We report on a spatial separated wavelength optical source for high density WDM application. Partially feedback diffracted spontaneous emission, able multiple lasing oscillations in erbium doped fiber medium. Each wavelength is spatially separated, showing narrow linewidth and stable oscillations. Four simultaneously wavelength operation was demonstrated. FWHM laser linewidth was measured to be as narrow as 1 GHz.

articleTitle: The vanishing modes - a fundamental concept in teaching microwaves

articleTitle: Application of signal processing algorithms in microwave applications
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The objective of this paper is to illustrate that the principle of analytic continuation can be utilized to interpolate/extrapolate either computational results or measured data in efficient fashion instead of utilizing sheer brute force.

articleTitle: Free space terahertz optoelectronics
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Free-space terahertz electro-optic sampling and magneto-optic sampling provide new methods for the measurement of freely-propagating pulsed electromagnetic radiation. Our recent experimental results of electro-optic detection of THz beams demonstrate an oscillation period of a mid-infrared THz beam as short as 31 fs. The upper-limit of frequency bandwidth reaches to 37 THz (8 /spl mu/m). We also demonstrate, for the first time, the concept and preliminary experimental results of a free-space ultrafast magneto-optic sampling system to measure propagating transient magnetic pulses.

articleTitle: Pulse position modulation (PPM) of ultrashort pulse trains in optical fibres
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Numerical simulations concerning the dynamical behaviour of infinite periodic trains of optical solitons subjected to modulation of the position of each soliton, in a single mode optical fibre, are presented. Long distance propagation of periodic patterns of 8 bit solitons, was simulated to study the pulse position-modulation (PPM) coding. A novel pulse configuration that may propagate long distances at normal dispersion regime, of the optical fibre, is proposed and simulated using the PPM coding.

articleTitle: Hybrid soliton pulses source with a 100 mm long chirped Bragg reflector
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: An external fibre Bragg grating cavity soliton pulse source with wide frequency operation range is demonstrated using an apodised 100 mm long step-chirped grating. Near transform-limited 50 ps pulses over a frequency range of 160 MHz around 1 GHz are obtained. Mode-locking and stable pulsing is demonstrated for the first time with such a long chirped grating.

articleTitle: An ultrawideband microwave phase shifter
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this paper, we present a new kind of high-frequency analog phase shifter suitable for ultrawide-band operation. Phase tuning is obtained with a local oscillator (LO) producing two coherent phase-shifted signals which are mixed with the incident radio-frequency (RF) signal. Measurements on a prototype exhibit a 20:1 operational bandwidth. We discuss system design rules and bandwidth limitations.

articleTitle: Humidity determination of hydrated media by a microwave technique
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This study proposes a humidity meter using a frequency of 9.4 GHz. The average medium water content, obtained by a non-destructive technique, gives instantly the humidity of a particular granulated volume of agricultural seeds. The laboratory and field studies, effected with various agricultural seeds, gave good results over a large range of humidity tested (7%<H/sub p/<60%). The measurements qualities depend essentially on how the calibration curves are obtained. The microwave measurements precision, compared with those done by classical drying methods, were close to 0.5% for high humidity rates. The humidity determination by a microwaves technique seems to be well adapted for a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: Trends in microwave photonics and related research at the Center for Microwave-Lightwave Engineering
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The rapid development of microwave and optical electronics over the past decades led to the natural merger of these important technologies, and microwave photonics emerged as a viable, exciting field of research with many potential areas of applications. This paper highlights some of the current and anticipated trends in microwave photonics. In particular, three areas are concentrated on: high speed fiberoptic links, optically controlled microwave devices and selected application areas. Emphasis is placed on research performed in the author's laboratory.

articleTitle: Multilayer analysis of anisotropic heat flux in vertical cavity surface emitting lasers with quarter wave semiconducting mirrors
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Temperature influences several properties of vertical cavity surface emitting lasers (VCSELs). Self heating restrains gain, raises threshold current and restricts output power. In this paper, thermal behaviour of VCSELs is evaluated with a procedure that includes multilayer aspects of heat flux propagation. The method takes into account the order between quarter-wave layers and can predict temperature profile inside the laser. Thermal resistance of typical devices calculated by using this approach is in good agreement with experimental values.

articleTitle: Effects of PMD with random mode coupling on 2.48 Gb/s IM-DD lightwave systems
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Effects of Polarization Mode Dispersion (PMD) on 2.48 Gb/s IM-DD lightwave systems are experimentally observed by using PMD emulators made with segments of highly birefringent fiber with random mode coupling splices. Random birefringence between mode couplings was also included in the emulator. The measurements indicate that the eye diagram is corrupted by PMD values above 10 ps. BER measurements show more than 1.5 dB power penalty for PMD values of 30 ps.

articleTitle: Design of optical decoder and optical address translator for high speed optical switching network
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this paper, the author studies the key technologies for the high speed optical switching network using the optical header/payload discriminator, optical decoder and optical address translator for header recognition, decoding and translating addresses directly in the optical domain. This system utilizes the optical ring resonator (ORR) for header/payload discriminator (OHPD). The optical delay line decoder (ODLD) and translator (OTR) for decoding and translating optical address for routing control are designed. For ODLD, the hierarchical prime code structure is designed with delay line logic to increase the channel capacity. For OTR, the optimal code mapping algorithm and serial or parallel code architectures are designed.

articleTitle: Development of CAE interface applied to optical fiber sensors simulation
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Optical fiber sensors require, sometimes, fibers with features very different from the commercially available ones. The required features for a particular sensing fiber depend upon the application, and can be determined with the help of software simulation tools. The use of CAE (Computer-Aided Engineering) tools for optical fiber sensor design can reduce the need of drawing several fibers to be tested in the laboratory, thus decreasing the costs in the sensor design. This work presents a specification for a prototype software tool, developed with concepts from existing models in software engineering and human-computer interaction. The prototype interface is implemented and existing simulation routines are incorporated into the simulation interface.

articleTitle: OTDM quasi-all-optical demultiplexing techniques comparative analysis
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This work compares recently developed demultiplexing OTDM techniques that use constructive and destructive interference approaches for channels switching. The techniques under analysis are the Mach-Zehnder Interferometer (MZI) and some of those operating in the fiber non-linear region, i.e.: Non-Linear-Optical Mirror (NOLM) Terahertz Optical Asymmetric Demultiplexer (TOAD) and Four Wave Mixing (FWM). The parameters used for comparison are the switching pulse power and temporal width, and the devices physical dimensions. It is shown that the TOAD offers the most advantageous results.

articleTitle: Speckle-free non-periodic Fresnel phase plates for beam shaping and optical interconnects
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Speckle-free non periodic near field Fresnel phase plates are designed using the iterative algorithm. This design is motivated by the potential use of those elements as beam shaping devices; to enhance the functionality of lasers cavities; and in optical interconnections between chips, fibers and waveguides. The elements were implemented using a phase-mostly liquid crystal television (LCTV) and photolithography process. Since the discrete Fourier transform in the computer design does not give full speckle pattern of the optically reconstructed image, the phase-mostly LCTV is useful for testing diffractive optical elements before the fabrication.

articleTitle: Analysis in 3-D of the complex and arbitrary bilateral finlines
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: An electromagnetic application is developed to obtain simultaneously the effective dielectric constant and the attenuation constant of arbitrary bilateral fin lines with semiconductor substrate and finite conductor thickness. Also the concise Transverse Transmission Line-TTL full wave method is used in the analysis. Results of the complex propagation as a function of the frequency and different dimensions and conductivity of the substrate, are obtained in 3-D.

articleTitle: Atmospheric laser propagation at 0.83 /spl mu/m over densely urbanised terrain
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: Results from propagation experiments at 0.83 /spl mu/m on a 4 km line-of-sight link across a densely urbanised area are presented and discussed. The experiments were carried out during the period 1992-1994 and concentrate on measurements of received intensity scintillations and angle of arrival. Results obtained provide information on the statistical and spectral characteristics of intensity scintillations and angle of arrival for near-saturated conditions, which can provide important information for the design of free-space digital optical links.

articleTitle: Synchronous fiber-optic code division multiple access networks with interference cancellations
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: In this paper, synchronous code division multiple access (S/CDMA) for the fiber-optic local area network (LAN) with interference cancellation schemes is investigated. We design the receiver structure for the S/CDMA with modified prime sequence codes, and the performance improvement through the employment of interference cancellation schemes is estimated. The results show that by using this scheme in the fiber-optic S/CDMA network, when shot noise and thermal noise are negligible, the influence of interference can be eliminated, and error free communications can also be achieved.

articleTitle: Progress on erbium-doped waveguide components
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The recent development in erbium-doped fiber amplifiers, and fiber lasers is reviewed. Also the latest results on planar erbium-doped waveguide amplifiers and high erbium concentration characterisation methods are presented.

articleTitle: PSAW and HVPSAW behaviour in layered structures
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: The Pseudo-SAWs (PSAW) have been extensively used since the 80's specially for high frequency SAW applications. The regular PSAW and the recently introduced High Velocity Pseudo-SAWs (HVPSAW), with phase velocities circa 40% (PSAW) and 100% (HVPSAW) higher than the phase velocities of the SAWs, permit the construction of higher frequency devices using the same photolithographic processes used for SAW devices. The resulting high frequency, high performance, and low loss devices have found immediate applications in communication equipment such as: cellular and mobile telephony, pagers, Local Area Networks (LANs), cordless phones, Global Positioning Systems (GPS), and security systems. Metallic layers are essential parts of all SAW devices, playing fundamental roles in the excitation, propagation, and reflection of the SAW signal. The careful analysis of the layered structure allows the understanding of the PSAW and HVPSAW relationship with higher order lossless SAW modes, also known as Generalized SAW modes (GSAW). This original analysis shows details of PSAWs' and HVPSAWs' transitions to GSAWs through some significant examples. The analysis includes original data regarding the different surface acoustic modes which coexist for a certain layer thickness and material, including the pseudo waves. The current study discuss how the field polarization, the estimated power flow angle (PFA), the power distribution with depth, and the electromechanical coupling coefficient behave with layer thickness and layer material for the referred modes. The results presented herein find immediate interest and application in the design of low loss, high performance, high frequency SAW devices for recent wireless applications (communication, remote sensing, security).

articleTitle: Antenna research and development in Canada
publicationTitle: 1997 SBMO/IEEE MTT-S International Microwave and Optoelectronics Conference. 'Linking to the Next Century'. Proceedings
abstract: This paper provides an overview of some of the major activities in the area of antennas carried out by Canadian scientists through individual efforts as well as through collaboration between universities, industry and governmental agencies.
